params.body:
## Why

The transactional mails were Laravel's stock markdown theme: `#3869d4` links, a `#2d3748` slate button, a centred logo, a grey `© ...` line. Only the logo had been changed. Every other surface of the app has moved to the house tokens in `resources/css/refresh.css`, so the mail is the one place a dealer still sees the framework default instead of Stocklist.

This gives the mails the same palette, the same button shape and the same two text levels (ink for headings, gray for body) without touching the 21 mail views: the whole change lives in the theme and the four components those views already render through.

## What

- **New theme** `resources/views/vendor/mail/html/themes/stocklist.css`, selected in `config/mail.php` (`markdown.theme => 'stocklist'`). Built from the refresh.css tokens, written out as literal hex because a mail cannot carry `var()`. 600px content on a `#f4f6f8` ground, white card, ink headings, gray body, brand blue as the single accent, table head like the app's list header, panel and subcopy in the same quiet register. Laravel's class names are kept, so `mail::button`, `mail::panel`, `mail::table` and `mail::subcopy` keep working unchanged.
- **Header** reworked: logo left on white, 3px brand-blue rule under it. No coloured band — a brand banner reads as marketing on a transactional mail, and the colour is worth more on the one button.
- **Footer** reworked: the three links the app footer carries (`ui.footer_manual`, `ui.footer_release_notes`, `mailto:contact@stocklistdealer.eu`), sender identity from `mail.from`, a line saying why the mail arrived, and a plain-text fallback line. Two new keys in `resources/lang/{nl,en}/ui.php`.
- **Button** is now bulletproof: the colour and padding sit on a `<td>`, not on the `<a>`. Outlook on Windows drops padding and background on a link, so the old styled `<a>` arrived there as a bare blue word.
- **Dark mode** in `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` inside the layout's `<style>` block, as overrides only — every colour is also defined in the light theme, because most clients ignore the block.
- **`stocklist:mail-preview`**: renders every mail view with fixed fake data to `storage/app/mail-preview/<name>.html` and prints the paths.

## Client compatibility choices

- **Where the CSS lives.** Laravel passes the theme file to `CssToInlineStyles` as a string; that file never reaches the client. Media queries and the dark scheme therefore have to live in the `<style>` block of `layout.blade.php`, which the inliner leaves in the document. The theme file holds only inline-able rules.
  - Worth knowing: the inliner's cleanup strips `@media …{…}` with a regex that matches **anywhere in the file, comments included**. A comment in the theme that merely mentioned the at-rule keyword swallowed the rule that followed, and the whole font stack silently went missing. There is now a comment in the file warning about it.
- **Dark rules carry `!important`**, because inline styles otherwise beat them.
- No webfonts (system stack with Arial/Helvetica fallback), no background images, no tracking pixel, no unsubscribe (these are transactional), tables for layout with `role="presentation"`, `<meta x-apple-disable-message-reformatting>`.
- Body text 15px (`p`, and 14px in `.table td`), links underlined, `alt` on the logo, headings with explicit colour and weight.
- Two breakpoints: 620px collapses the 600px card and tightens the padding; 500px makes the button full width.
- `.button-stocklist`, `.btn`/`.btn-primary` and the `success`/`error`/`primary`/`blue`/`green`/`red` variants are all defined, because the views ask for all of them. A bare `<a class="button button-…">` in a view (lead, worklist) gets the shape through borders; inside `mail::button` the link gets `button-inner`, which hands the padding back to the `<td>`.
- A message can now set a preheader with `@slot('preheader')`; without it nothing is emitted.

## Preview command

```bash
php artisan stocklist:mail-preview                # all of them
php artisan stocklist:mail-preview --only=export_mail
php artisan stocklist:mail-preview --path=/tmp/mails
open storage/app/mail-preview/*.html
```

It renders only: no `Mail::send` anywhere in the command, no database read (every model is an unsaved instance with hand-set relations), and the `vehicles` disk is pointed at an empty local folder for the run, because `export_daily_mail` asks `Storage::disk('vehicles')->exists(...)` and that is an S3 call per car. `AppServiceProvider`'s `Mail::alwaysTo` and `Outbound::seal()` are untouched.

## Which mails checked

All 26 views render, 0 failures (21 in `mails/`, minus the two partials, plus the 6 in `mails/transport/`):

`bought_email`, `default`, `export_almost_expired_mail`, `export_controlled`, `export_daily_mail`, `export_ended_mail`, `export_expired_mail`, `export_mail`, `export_mail_lost`, `export_mail_won`, `generalException`, `lead`, `open_worklist_items`, `real-garant-history`, `resend_export_mail`, `sold_email`, `test`, `transport`, `transport/paid`, `transport/paid_admin`, `transport/paid_seller`, `transport/price_available`, `transport/price_requested`, `transport/price_requested_admin`, `vehicle-proposal`, `vehicle_delivered`.

`export_vehicle` and `export_dealer` are partials without their own wrapper; they are covered through the six mails that `@include` them.

Nothing needed data that could not be faked. Two notes on the fixtures: photos point at paths that do not exist, so the preview shows a broken image where a car photo would be (the mail itself is fine — it is the same URL the app serves); and `transport` needs `pickUpCountry`/`deliveryCountry` set, because `getPickUpAddressAttribute()` reads `->name` on them without a null guard.

### One view changed, and why

`resources/views/mails/open_worklist_items.blade.php`, one condition:

```diff
-@if(($showTransport ?? false) && isset($openTransport) && $openTransport > 0)
+@if(($showTransport ?? false) && isset($openTransport) && is_countable($openTransport) && count($openTransport) > 0)
```

`OpenWorklistItemsEmail` passes `$dealer->OpenTransport`, which is a relation and therefore a `Collection`. `Collection > 0` throws "could not be converted to int", so this branch fataled for every recipient with `showTransport` true (role BEHEERDER). It is a pre-existing bug, not one the styling introduced, but it blocked the preview and the fix is one condition. No wording or content changed in any view.

## Verification

- `./vendor/bin/phpunit --filter='Mail|Export|SmokeTest|ClassReferencesResolve'` → OK (137 tests, 202 assertions), against a local MySQL loaded the way CI does it.
- `php artisan view:cache` → all 414 compiled views `php -l` clean.
- `php artisan stocklist:mail-preview` → 26 rendered, 0 failed; opened and read in a browser at 900px and at the 620/500 breakpoints.
params.title: Mails: the house style, and a way to see them all
